notes: Worked-example diagrams show only what the example gives (question side, token after the question text).
Solution diagrams are required only where the solution adds a construction, an arrangement or a highlight that carries meaning; arithmetic on the given figure is optional/none.
Teaching images of the same figures stay in the plan and are never linked; every item that needs a figure has its own diagram.

both diagonals pass through (4,3), the midpoint of each

items.reason: The two heights AX and BY and the sides they stand on are placed only by the picture of triangle ABC.

diagram.manim_description: Draw triangle ABC in INK (no fill), to scale with 1 unit = 1 length unit: B=(0,0), C=(5,0), A=(2.354,3). Draw the segment BY as a solid INK segment from B to Y=(2.812,2.48) on side AC and put a small INK right-angle square (side 0.25) at Y between YB and YC. Do not write any length on BY. Letters in INK: A above A, B below and to the left of B, C below and to the right of C, X below X, Y above and to the right of Y. GUIDE dimension arrows with double arrowheads and thin GUIDE extension lines: (1) a vertical arrow at x=-0.7 from y=0 to y=3 (extension lines from B and from A), label '3' to its left; (2) a horizontal arrow at y=-0.8 from x=0 to x=5 (extension lines from B and C), label '5' centred under it; (3) an arrow parallel to AC, shifted 0.6 units outward (up and to the right) from (2.804,3.397) to (5.45,0.397) with extension lines from A and C, and the label '4' written along it (rotated to the slope of AC) just above the arrow at its middle.
accuracy_checks: AX = 3, BC = 5, AC = 4 hold for the coordinates (AC = 4.000)
BY drawn perpendicular to AC (BY·AC direction = 0)
the length of BY is NOT shown (it is the unknown)
area check: 1/2 x 5 x 3 = 7.5 = 1/2 x 4 x BY gives BY = 3.75 (not drawn)
diagram.alt_text: Triangle ABC with base BC = 5, height AX = 3, side AC = 4, and a perpendicular BY dropped from B to AC.

items.lp_book_number: Using the Area Formula: finding the height BY

items.lp_book_number: Figure it Out (Triangles), Q6
items.ncert_ref: chapter p.11 - Figure it Out, Triangles Q6
items.question_text: ABCD, BCEF and BFGH are identical squares, with H directly above B. The red region is the triangle DCH and the blue region is the part of square ABCD to the left of the line DH. (i) If the area of the red region is 49 sq. units, what is the area of the blue region? (ii) In another version, if the blue and red regions together are 180 sq. units, what is the area of each square?
items.reason: Positions of the three squares, the line DH and the red and blue regions exist only in the picture (colour carries the meaning).

diagram.manim_description: Work in unit coordinates, side of each square = 1, to scale, outlines INK 3 px. Draw three identical squares: ABCD with A=(0,1), B=(1,1), C=(1,0), D=(0,0); BCEF with B=(1,1), C=(1,0), E=(2,0), F=(2,1); BFGH with B=(1,1), F=(2,1), G=(2,2), H=(1,2). So ABCD is bottom-left, BCEF is to its right and BFGH sits on top of BCEF with H directly above B. Fill triangle D-C-H, vertices (0,0), (1,0), (1,2), with RED = #D55E00 (the palette vermilion, used here only as the red of the question's red region). Fill triangle with vertices (0,0), (0,1), (0.5,1) with BLUE = SET_A #0072B2. The other regions stay white. Draw the segment from D=(0,0) to H=(1,2) in INK on top of the fills; it crosses AB at (0.5,1). Redraw the square outlines above the fills. Letters in INK: H above and to the left of H, G above and to the right of G, A to the left of A, B just above and to the right of B, F to the right of F, C just below and to the right of C, D below and to the left of D, E below and to the right of E.
accuracy_checks: red triangle DCH has base 1 and height 2, area 1 = one square
line DH meets AB at (0.5,1), the midpoint of AB
blue triangle has legs 1 and 0.5, area 0.25 = a quarter of a square
H is directly above B
diagram.alt_text: Three identical squares in an L shape with a red triangle DCH and a blue triangle at the left of the first square cut by the line DH.
diagram.render_note: Book p.11 Q6 figure. 'Red' is drawn with the palette vermilion #D55E00 and 'blue' with SET_A so the picture agrees with the words red region / blue region in the question.

items.lp_book_number: Figure it Out (Triangles), Q6
items.ncert_ref: chapter p.11 - Figure it Out, Triangles Q6
items.question_text: ABCD, BCEF and BFGH are identical squares, with H directly above B. The red region is the triangle DCH and the blue region is the part of square ABCD to the left of the line DH. (i) If the area of the red region is 49 sq. units, what is the area of the blue region? (ii) In another version, if the blue and red regions together are 180 sq. units, what is the area of each square?
items.reason: The steps rest on facts that are visible only in the figure: DH crosses AB at its midpoint, the legs are s and s/2, the red base and height are s and 2s; the figure adds the midpoint and the lengths.

diagram.manim_description: Redraw the question figure exactly as it is (same squares, letters, line DH, red and blue fills, same positions and colours), then add in ANSWER green #009E73: (1) a filled dot at M=(0.5,1), where DH crosses AB, with one short tick on AM and one short tick on MB; (2) a GUIDE-style double-headed dimension arrow below DC at y=-0.35 from x=0 to x=1 with the label 's' centred under it; (3) a double-headed dimension arrow at x=-0.35 from y=0 to y=1 (left of AD) with the label 's' to its left; (4) a double-headed dimension arrow above AM at y=1.3 from x=0 to x=0.5 with the label 's/2' above it; (5) a double-headed dimension arrow at x=2.35 from y=0 to y=2 (right of the right-hand column) with the label '2s' to its right; (6) the label 's²' inside the red triangle centred at (0.68,0.42) and the label 's²/4' inside the blue triangle centred at (0.2,0.82). Dimension arrows and labels are drawn in ANSWER green, with thin extension lines in GUIDE; every label sits on a small BG plate so lines do not cross it.
accuracy_checks: red area = 1/2 x s x 2s = s²
DH rises 2s over a run of s, so at height s (side AB) it is at x = s/2: the midpoint of AB
blue area = 1/2 x s x s/2 = s²/4
s²/4 + s² = 5s²/4: 49/4 = 12.25 for (i); 5s²/4 = 180 gives s² = 144 for (ii) (not drawn)
diagram.alt_text: The three squares with the line DH crossing AB at its midpoint; sides marked s, s/2 and 2s, the red triangle s² and the blue triangle s²/4.
diagram.render_note: Same layout as the question figure; only symbolic lengths, as the LP steps use s for the side.
